result.title: Concealed Handgun Detection using WiFi Signals
result.summary: While conventional camera-based surveillance systems and metal detectors can provide a sufficient level of security when used appropriately, they have fundamental limitations that reduce their applicability. Camera-based systems are unable to detect occluded or concealed threats and metal detectors require each person to enter through a narrow opening one at a time, leading to congestion issues and limited use in large crowds. A WiFi-based security system has the potential to be a complementary modality that is able to handle occlusions or concealment and is not hindered by strict spatial configurations. In this paper, we propose use Channel State Information estimated from WiFi-signals to detect concealed handguns. To this end we collect a dataset of aligned WiFi signals and RGB images that we call the WiFire dataset. We also propose a deep learning model called WiFireNet tailored to detect concealed handguns in WiFi signals using vision-based supervision signals. Our results show that concealed handgun detection is possible in WiFi and has promise as a complementary modality to surveillance cameras and metal detectors. We release the dataset, model and code to facilitate the further research into WiFi-based handgun detection.

AI.relevance_reason: 该工作研究用 WiFi 信道状态信息检测隐匿枪支，并以 RGB 视觉信号作监督训练检测模型，属于新的感知模态与物理层安全应用，不涉及 VLM 推理状态、latent 表示生成或推理期决策，也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的具体方法线索；「视觉监督非视觉模态」仅是模态对齐，与研究关注的视觉证据保留和推理状态使用无实质联系。
